title: Salt Lake (Tuz Gölü) & Silk Road Caravanserais Route
seoTitle: Salt Lake (Tuz Gölü) & Silk Road Caravanserais Route
metaDescription: Time Tuz Gölü's mirror season, add 13th-century Sultanhanı Caravanserai on the Cappadocia drive, pack right for salt flats, and weigh Ankara detours.
quickAnswer: Tuz Gölü turns into a sky-reflecting mirror from April to June when shallow water blankets the basin, before drying into a walkable white and rose-tinted salt crust between July and September. Combine the shoreline with 13th-century Sultanhanı Caravanserai on a single Silk Road drive linking Ankara, Konya, and Cappadocia.

body.text: Sprawling across the meeting point of Ankara, Aksaray, and Konya provinces, [Lake Tuz (Tuz Gölü)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Tuz) is Türkiye's second-largest lake and a protected [UNESCO Tentative List](https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/tr/) wetland. On its own, it is a striking 45-minute stop; paired with the fortified Seljuk Silk Road inns along the D300 highway, it turns a central Anatolian transit day into a memorable overland route.
Which months turn Tuz Gölü into a mirror?

Spring—specifically April through early June—delivers Tuz Gölü's classic sky-mirror effect, when winter rainfall and snowmelt leave a calm, ankle-deep sheet of water across the flat salt pan, as documented in [seasonal Tuz Gölü guides](https://traveltourshop.com/blog/tuz-golu-salt-lake-travel-guide). By late June through September, intense evaporation hardens the surface into a dry white salt crust.

body.text: Many travelers expect glowing pink water year-round and leave disappointed in May. As [Cappadocia Salt Lake field notes](https://visitcappadocia.net/en/blog/cappadocias-best-salt-lakes-and-flamingos-a-guide) explain, the rose-to-coral tint peaks in July–September when high salinity triggers beta-carotene production in Dunaliella salina microalgae. Arrive near sunrise or late afternoon; harsh midday sun flattens both reflections and color.
How do you add Sultanhanı Caravanserai on the drive to Cappadocia?

[Sultanhanı Caravanserai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sultan_Han) sits directly along the D300 highway 40 kilometers west of Aksaray, adding under 30 minutes of detour time on the drive between [Konya](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/konya-travel-guide) and Cappadocia. Commissioned in 1229 by Seljuk Sultan Alaeddin Keykubat I, it is Anatolia's largest surviving Silk Road roadside fortress.

Listed on the UNESCO Tentative List under Seljuk Caravanserais per [TÜRSAB visitor notices](https://www.tursab.org.tr/duyurular/sultanhani-kervansarayi-ziyaret-saatleri-hakkinda-duyuru), Sultanhanı opens daily (roughly 08:00–19:00 in summer and 08:30–17:30 in winter, per [2026 visitor reports](https://hobletsonthego.com/where-weve-been/europe/turkey/sultanhani-caravanserai/)). Plan 45 to 60 minutes to examine the towering carved marble muqarnas entrance portal, the raised courtyard kiosk mosque, and the vaulted winter hall where medieval merchants sheltered camels and silk bales free of charge for three nights. If you have an extra half hour, add nearby Ağzıkarahan Caravanserai 15 kilometers east of Aksaray on the road toward Nevşehir.
What should you wear for walking on salt flats?

Wear cheap rubber flip-flops, waterproof sandals, or walk barefoot, and bring a two-liter bottle of fresh tap water plus a small towel in your car trunk. Brine and razor-sharp salt crystals permanently stain leather, suede, and mesh sneakers—and crusted salt stings minor cuts on bare ankles.

items: Footwear: Waterproof rubber sandals or barefoot; never wear good leather boots or white fabric trainers onto the crust.
Eye and skin protection: Polarized sunglasses and high-SPF sunscreen are mandatory—white salt reflects UV light upward like fresh snow.
Clothing: Roll-up trousers or shorts that will not wick salty brine above the knee, plus a light windbreaker for exposed plateau gusts.
Cleanup: Rinse feet thoroughly at the roadside rest-stop taps or with your own water bottle before getting back into the car.

body.text: Is a detour from Ankara worth the drive?

As a standalone out-and-back excursion from [Ankara](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/ankara-travel-guide), Tuz Gölü requires a 130-to-154-kilometer drive each way to the Şereflikoçhisar viewing area—roughly 90 minutes per leg on the D750/O-21 corridor per [Rome2Rio estimates](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Ankara/%C5%9Eerefliko%C3%A7hisar). For most travelers, three hours of highway driving purely for a 45-minute lake stop is a poor trade.

The detour becomes genuinely worthwhile when you use Tuz Gölü as a natural waypoint on a one-way drive from Ankara to Cappadocia (roughly 3.5 to 4 hours total driving), or when you loop south through Aksaray to combine the salt flats with Ihlara Valley and Sultanhanı Caravanserai. If you are flying between Istanbul and Cappadocia instead, you can visit Tuz Gölü as a late-afternoon sunset excursion from Göreme (around 90 minutes each way) without doubling back to Ankara.

faq.q: Is there an entrance fee to visit Tuz Gölü?
faq.a: Walking onto the salt lake at the main Şereflikoçhisar roadside viewing facilities is free, though small rest stops may charge a modest parking or foot-rinse fee.

faq.q: When can you see flamingos at Tuz Gölü?
faq.a: Greater flamingos nest in protected southern and central parts of the basin from spring through mid-summer. Keep respectful distance and bring binoculars—entering nesting zones disturbs the colony.

faq.q: Can you drive a rental car onto the Tuz Gölü salt flats?
faq.a: No. Driving onto the salt crust risks sinking into hidden mud pockets, damages the protected wetland, and corrodes vehicle undercarriages. Park at designated roadside lots and walk in on foot.

faq.q: How far is Tuz Gölü from Göreme in Cappadocia?
faq.a: The southern shoreline near Aksaray and Şereflikoçhisar sits roughly 110 to 130 kilometers northwest of Göreme, about 1 hour 30 minutes to 1 hour 45 minutes by car.

faq.q: Are there other Seljuk caravanserais near Sultanhanı?
faq.a: Yes. Ağzıkarahan Caravanserai lies 15 kilometers northeast of Aksaray along the road toward Cappadocia, and Sarıhan Caravanserai sits near Avanos—all built during the 13th-century Seljuk trade boom.

faq.q: Is Tuz Gölü worth visiting in winter?
faq.a: Only if you are already driving past between Ankara and Cappadocia. Cold winds, higher water levels, and muddy edges prevent walking far onto the flats between November and March.
